thread:
Incident Bot: Pager: SLA breach detected for tenant MapFlow (SLA: 99.9% p99 latency). Trigger: mapgen-service p99 > 1200ms for 7m. @on-call Sam Carter // paging level: P1
Sam Carter: got it, looking
Sam Carter: jumping into logs and metrics now, assigning Priya for infra checks
Priya Nair: on it — checking node scatter and recent deploys
monitoring-bot: Alert details: rule_id=alert_sla_mapflow_p99_v2, scope=tenant.mapflow, count=1, avg_latency=1350ms, last_eval=now
Sam Carter: mapgen CPU across cluster normal. Not a host OOM. I see bursts in request concurrency from a single client IP range — looks like a large backfill job from MapFlow?
Marta Chen: MapFlow CS confirms they kicked a large import a few minutes ago. They said they expected some spike but not page.
Sam Carter: ok, two tracks: 1) mitigate pages/noise so on-call can keep focus; 2) fix alerting to be tenant-aware and avoid false SLA trips for scheduled heavy jobs.
Lena Ortiz: prioritize mitigation first. If this is customer-initiated load, we should silence tenant-level SLA pages and instead use a softer ticketing alert.
Sam Carter: I am going to silence the tenant SLA alert for MapFlow for 30 minutes while we monitor. Doing: `alertctl mute --rule alert_sla_mapflow_p99_v2 --scope tenant.mapflow --for 30m --reason "customer import spike"`
monitoring-bot: Command accepted. Rule muted for 30m. Owner: on-call Sam Carter.
Priya Nair: also enabling a quick dashboard panel to show per-tenant p95/p99 and top client IPs: `dash create mapflow-temp-panel --queries "p99(latency) by tenant, top(client_ip)"`
Sam Carter: good. Adding a temporary rate-limit on unauthenticated ingest endpoints for MapFlow's tenant to reduce burst: `routectl set-rate-limit --tenant mapflow --path /v1/mapgen/ingest --rps 50`
monitoring-bot: Rate limit applied. Note: this will add 5xx on throttled requests — watch for customer complaints.
Marta Chen: told MapFlow CS about the mitigation and request they retry with backoff. They acked and will spread the import.
Jamal Abbas: I'm taking the overnight handoff at 00:30 UTC. If the muted alert still sees p99 > 2000ms but overall user impact persists, escalate back to P1.
Sam Carter: handoff noted. Current plan: unmute only if true user-facing errors increase, otherwise let this be an operational event and follow up with tuning.
Priya Nair: initial root cause notes: customer-triggered high-concurrency import + our alert rule evaluated p99 across rolling window without suppressing for scheduled jobs. This made the tenant-specific SLA rule too sensitive to transient batch jobs.
Lena Ortiz: post-incident actions — create task list here and assign owners.
Sam Carter: action items I propose: 1) Replace hard p99 threshold with sustained-window check (p99 > threshold for 15m after smoothing) for tenant SLA alerts — owner: Priya; 2) Add scheduled-job tag suppression: if tenant has active long-running import flag, route to non-paged alerting — owner: Marta; 3) Build per-tenant spike dashboard and add runbook links — owner: Jamal; 4) Update runbooks and add example `alertctl` commands for quick muting — owner: Sam; 5) Postmortem doc and timeline — owner: Lena.
Marta Chen: will add a customer-visible note template for CS so they can proactively message customers when we apply temporary throttles/mutes.
Priya Nair: quick snippet for changed alert rule to avoid noisy pages: ```yaml
alert: TenantP99Sustained
expr: increase(p99_latency{tenant="$tenant"}[5m]) > 0 and p99_latency{tenant="$tenant"} > 1200
for: 15m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Tenant {{ $labels.tenant }} sustained p99 > 1200ms"
```
Sam Carter: that looks good — add grouping by job_type to ignore scheduled imports (we'll need a label on those requests).
Lena Ortiz: timeline: please capture events and exact command outputs in the incident doc. We will review at next on-call retrospective.
Jamal Abbas: I'll own the dashboard + runbook items during my overnight shift and follow up in the ticket.
Sam Carter: will convert this thread into a short post-incident note and create GH issues for the action items.
monitoring-bot: Created ticket #INF-4821 "Tenant SLA alert: add sustained-window + scheduled import suppression" and assigned to Priya Nair.
Sam Carter: closing immediate paging loop — will leave mute in place for 30m. If anything changes, ping @on-call. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Marta Chen: thanks @Sam and Priya — CS will reach out to MapFlow with the template when/if needed.
Lena Ortiz: great coordination. We'll aim to reduce noisy tenant-specific pages by >80% with the new rule changes and dashboard.
Jamal Abbas: noted for handoff. Night on-call out.
Incident Bot: Thread closed by Sam Carter at 1769124300
